items.description: Average annual energy used for cooking per New Zealand house, all cooking appliances and fuels (gross energy)
items.note: 900 kWh (SE 60) is the national 'All cooking' average; 620-1,090 the regional averages. Averaged over all houses and fuels, mostly electric, so it is not a gas-stove figure; ranges use about 50% more in winter than in summer.

items.description: Net calorific value and carbon content of liquefied petroleum gas
items.note: IPCC gives TJ/Gg, equal to MJ/kg.

items.description: Bottled LPG installed at a typical New Zealand home
items.note: A supplier's page, not a survey.

items.description: Fuelwood a household cooking on traditional fires burns per adult equivalent fed, measured by kitchen performance tests
items.unit: kg per adult equivalent per day
items.note: Non-adopter households (traditional three-stone fires), 25 each. desta2020 Table 7: 8.34 +/- 2.20 kg per household per day for 5.14 +/- 1.49 adult equivalents served, '1.74' kg/AME/day; wood 'pre-weighed at the beginning of the day and the remaining wood was weighed at the end of the day'. kefalew2021 Table 6: 10.5 +/- 3.83 kg per household per day for 5.07 +/- 1.47 adult equivalents, 1.98 +/- 0.58 kg/AME/day. Adult equivalents follow FAO's wood-fuel survey weights (Openshaw). The wood's moisture is not stated; it is used as the store's air-dry wood. Rural Ethiopian households, not New Zealand ones.

items.description: Gross solid-fuel energy a year in New Zealand houses that use solid fuel for each end-use
items.note: Rows are SR155 Table 3's 'Range - solid fuel', 'Other heating - solid fuel' and 'Wetback - solid fuel'; gross energy, the wood's energy before the appliance's losses. Each is the mean over houses with that end-use, so one house with all three is their sum.

items.description: Net calorific value of air-dry firewood at about 25% moisture (oven-dry basis)
items.note: SR141 gives 14.5 MJ/kg, about 4.0 kWh/kg, for air-dry wood; dry wood is 18.7 MJ/kg. HEEP itself adopted 3.5 kWh/kg assuming a quarter of the wood is fresh-cut; the store's wood is seasoned (D40).
